stories.headline: AI/tech rout gives the Nasdaq its worst week since June; VIX hits a four-month high
stories.blurb: The Nasdaq fell 2.1% on Friday and about 4.5% on the week as worries about returns on AI spending and debt-heavy data-center players (CoreWeave −12% on the day) spread. The S&P 500 lost 1.1% and closed below its 50-day average; the VIX closed near 20. — BTC has been trading with tech this month; a deeper equity sell-off is the most direct path to a second $80k test.

stories.headline: Oil breaks $100 on Middle East and Russia supply worries
stories.blurb: WTI settled up about 3.5% near $101 and Brent near $110 after reports of a possible problem near Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, a Russian refinery outage and rising U.S.–Iran tensions. Crude is up roughly 8% WoW. — Energy drove September's hot CPI; $100 oil keeps a December Fed hike in play and squeezes the case for lower yields that rescued crypto mid-week.

stories.headline: Warsh gives no new signal; October hike odds keep cooling
stories.blurb: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at an IMF event in Bangkok without commenting on a year-end hike. CME FedWatch, as cited by CNBC, shows about an 82% chance the Fed holds at the Oct 27–28 meeting. — A quiet Fed removes one near-term shock; the risk now sits with oil and the next inflation data, not Fed-speak.

stories.headline: Bitcoin ETF selling slows to about a quarter of last week's pace
stories.blurb: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $146M Monday to Thursday, with Friday tracking a small outflow (IBIT still pending), after about $681M of outflows the week before. October is net negative by roughly $535M through Thursday. CoinShares counted $434M of weekly outflows across crypto funds. — Demand is still not buying the dip, but forced-feeling redemptions have eased — the floor is less fragile than a week ago.

stories.headline: Futures flip back to leverage building into weakness
stories.blurb: CheckOnChain's futures OI vs price scatter moved from Spot Rally to Leveraged Sell-Off as of Oct 16: seven-day open interest is up about 2.7% while price is down about 1%, with funding still positive. — New leverage on a falling price adds liquidation fuel — a break below $80k could move fast, and so could a short squeeze if $84k breaks.

daily_focus.text: What changed this week: hot CPI and PPI, then Friday's AI/tech sell-off and $100 oil, gave BTC a second losing week (−1.8% WoW, still +6.6% MoM). It fell less than the Nasdaq and kept $80k. ETF outflows shrank to about a quarter of last week's, and October hike odds cooled after a quiet Warsh. The worry: futures open interest is rising while price falls, so a break of $80k could cascade. ~$80k below and ~$84k above frame the week.
